product_from_film: Pulse links organic content, leads and revenue in an attribution dashboard.
explains_well: The question about which video brought a lead becomes a content table and contact history.
unclear: The film does not show how tracking is installed or how attribution is verified.
scenario: Find which content produced a lead, then inspect that lead’s earlier steps.
product_clear_basis: At 12–13s, track conversions and organic content sit beside the dashboard.

scenes.action: Black gives way to a warm-lead count, a creator with notification cards, then a question and two different creator-video cards. Green fills occupy the cards before the Pulse name.
scenes.design: White type on black; green blocks and glows; creator photographs.
scenes.purpose: Connect a business result to uncertainty about its source.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–10s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Pulse name changes to white overview screens, content list and source revenue cards. A connected source diagram appears at 18–19s before overview returns.
scenes.design: Green graph and selected labels; social icons connect to a target on a white canvas.
scenes.purpose: Introduce conversion tracking and its source setup.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 10–22s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The views sentence changes to a content table; one row stands forward at 26s. Large sidebar and source revenue cards follow.
scenes.design: Highlighted row has a green halo; short phrases sit beside cropped UI.
scenes.purpose: Move attention from view counts to money-producing content.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 22–29s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Contacts overview becomes a booked-call card, then a table with one contact’s history. That panel occupies the right half as explanatory text appears left.
scenes.design: White contact panel against a green lower glow; colored tags are secondary.
scenes.purpose: Show the earlier steps behind one lead.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 29–39s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Click, lead, call and customer counts form a horizontal chain. Agency text leads to a workspace form, another overview and a payment card.
scenes.design: Black metric capsules and green arrows; white form fields.
scenes.purpose: Extend attribution to an agency workspace and financial outcome.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 39–47s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Green rings surround the brand dot, then Pulse and its tracking phrase appear on black. A free-trial sentence follows, ending black.
scenes.design: Green dot, glow panel and highlighted free-trial phrase.
scenes.purpose: Return to brand and give a next step.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 47–52.033s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: A lead-source question leads to overview, content revenue, contact history and an agency extension.
0s is black; at 1s a small lead-count sentence appears, with an enlarged green count block at 2s. The context arrives at 3s.
Organic-content conversion tracking is clear by 13s. The agency audience is explicit at 42s.
UI crops change scale; one content row and one history panel are isolated. Exact movement paths and easing remain unknown.
Black question screens become a white demo near 10–11s; the green motif connects them. The sampled frames do not establish the transition mechanism.
Green light and halos pick out useful objects on otherwise flat white and black fields.
Large explanation carries meaning, while detailed table text is secondary. The metric chain makes conversion steps larger than the tables.
Voice delivery is unverified.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Two creator images frame the opening choice; the main proof uses UI panels and a simple network diagram. Asset origin is unknown.
Source duration 52.033 s; Watch metadata 1920 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: The large text and UI sequence convey content attribution without speech; setup details are still missing.
Green pulls attention to a word, table row or arrow. The isolated contact panel makes its relationship to the left-hand explanation clear.
The 39–46s section adds conversion rates, agency support, workspace creation and payment in a short span.
categories.experiment: Give the agency workspace its own short follow-up film.

categories.finding: The opening asks which video sent the lead. Content revenue and contact history answer that idea; the ending gives a free trial.
The film appears to move from uncertainty to confidence through clearer tables and a payment card. This is an interpretation, not a viewer result.
categories.reason: Emotion is inferred from the sequence.

categories.finding: The green accent and repeated overview connect the modules, but a single named lead is not carried from the opening to the final payment.
Attribution screens and a workspace form are shown. Correct tracking and real revenue are claims, not independently tested behavior.
The green circle returns as the Pulse mark; the attribution network and contact history give more specificity than the generic revenue graph.
The contact history adds a useful explanation. The late agency detour is less necessary to resolve the original lead-source question.
For Tin, isolate one workflow row and then one run history panel. Use actual UI states, the same campaign name and a reserved accent.
categories.experiment: Build a campaign → booked lead sequence with one highlighted row.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Lift one meaningful UI row out of a dense table, then show its detail panel.
try: For Tin attribution, show two posts, ask which produced a lead, and open the matching tracked lead using three prepared UI states.
For Tin workflow proof, retain one campaign name from overview through run history to its output; use one accent color for that path.
lessons.avoid: Adding an agency workspace and payment before the main attribution example has a named, traceable result.
lessons.open: Installation steps, real attribution accuracy, sound and exact transition paths remain unverified.

comparison.story: Lead-source question → conversion dashboard → content and lead history → agency workspace → trial.
comparison.motion: Scale changes and isolated UI layers across 10–46s; exact motion between samples unverified.
comparison.sound: ASR draft supports a lead-attribution explanation; voice delivery, music and effects unverified.
comparison.texture: Black/white fields, saturated green glows and creator images; asset provenance unknown.
comparison.lesson: Make a dense table readable by isolating the row that answers the opening question.
